# routine { #wdm.routine }

`routine`

A minimal, current-state definition of a lifting routine.

Where the workout tracker spreadsheet (`wdm.exercise`,
`wdm.tracker_write`) is a growing, dated log -- one full block of rows
per session, every time it happens -- this is the opposite: one row per
*exercise*, one definition per named session ("Lower A"), overwritten in
place whenever the routine actually changes.

It exists for a workflow where the routine is defined once and referred to by
name on the days it's repeated -- "did Lower A today" -- with the day-by-day
record living in ``observations.csv`` (its ``exercise_kcal`` column, and
optionally a note naming the session) rather than in a spreadsheet that would
otherwise need a new dated block appended every session. That is a real
alternative to `wdm.tracker_write`'s approach, not a replacement for it:
this file has no history, so if a session's kcal estimate matters historically
-- did last month's Lower A cost less because you had lighter weights then --
the dated tracker is still the right tool. For a routine held roughly constant
and referred to by name, this is simpler.

Reuses the MET table, tempo parsing, and rest-period assumptions from
`wdm.exercise`; only the source of the sets, and how they're grouped
(per exercise, not per set), differs.

## Classes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [RoutineEstimate](#wdm.routine.RoutineEstimate) | Estimated energy cost of one named session, from its routine definition. |

### RoutineEstimate { #wdm.routine.RoutineEstimate }

```python
routine.RoutineEstimate(session, kcal, n_sets, duration_min)
```

Estimated energy cost of one named session, from its routine definition.

Carries no date -- a routine definition is a standing fact, not an event.
Attach whichever date it applies to yourself, when logging it.

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |

### estimate_named_session_kcal { #wdm.routine.estimate_named_session_kcal }

```python
routine.estimate_named_session_kcal(routine, session, weight_lb)
```

Estimate a named session's kcal cost from the routine definition.

Unlike the tracker's date-grouped estimate, there is exactly one
definition per session name here, so no "most recent instance" lookup is
needed -- this either finds the session or it does not.

### list_sessions { #wdm.routine.list_sessions }

```python
routine.list_sessions(routine)
```

Distinct session names defined in the routine, in file order.

### load_routine { #wdm.routine.load_routine }

```python
routine.load_routine(path)
```

Read a routine CSV: one row per exercise, not per set.

Expected columns: ``session, exercise, sets, reps, weight_lb, tempo,
category, notes``. ``reps`` and ``weight_lb`` may be blank for bodyweight
or isometric exercises. ``category`` is specified directly as one of
``compound`` / ``isolation`` / ``core`` -- a routine of this size does not
need the tracker's Muscle-Guide-driven inference, and specifying it
directly means there is no join to silently miss.
